title: Memory of Oceania, after Matisse, Surfaces

said.q: Muniz’s “Memory of Oceania, after Matisse, Surfaces” begins with photographs of painted surfaces that are then cut and collaged, in several three-dimensional layers. This distance between the original painted surface and the final representative object invokes both a “material gain and virtual loss” for the viewer, as their experience of the physical work of art is recontextualized by additional modes of image production and representation.
